page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz, the instance supplies 16 dedicated physical cores mapped 1:1 without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 64 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an 80 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware cryptographic acceleration enabled via standard AES instructions.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory subsystem throughput and robust multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in the PassMark memory suite alongside top-quartile performance in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth (259.29 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (113.31 GB/sec). Multi-core processing capability is reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,780.0 and strong database operation throughput on PassMark. Single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng and bzip3 decompression, consistently fall within the middle 50% percentile across comparable cloud servers.

The instance relies exclusively on network-attached block storage, as bundled local NVMe storage is omitted. GPU acceleration is not present, making it unsuitable for GPU-dependent training or hardware-accelerated graphics pipelines. However, having fully dedicated cores without hyperthreading eliminates thread contention, delivering reliable performance per vCPU for sustained multi-threaded workloads.

Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16 represents a cost-efficient resource tier for mid-sized containerized services, application middleware, data processing pipelines, and relational database hosting where high memory bandwidth and predictable multi-threaded Arm compute are required.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16 is a general-purpose ARM-based virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 64 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 platform clocked at 3.0 GHz with an 80 MB L3 cache, the system eliminates thread contention by running without simultaneous multithreading. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier memory performance, characterized by high uncached read and write bandwidth, alongside top-quartile Geekbench multi-core and PassMark database processing results. The instance contains no bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. With balanced resource density and consistent per-core execution, it serves efficiently as a platform for backend web serving, relational databases, data pipelines, and containerized microservices.
